sections.h2: Which Fulton County office records my deed?
sections.html:
Deeds for Fulton County property are recorded and indexed by the clerk's Real Estate Division, part of the office of the Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts. It also handles lien filings, plats, condominium floor plans, military discharges, partnerships, trade names and Uniform Commercial Code filings.

The Deeds and Records Room sits on the ground floor of the Lewis Slaton Courthouse in Atlanta and holds instruments that reach back to the early 1800s. The Real Estate Recording customer service line is (404) 613-5313. Mail for the Record Room goes to 136 Pryor St., CG13, Atlanta, GA 30303.

sections.h2: How fast does the Fulton County clerk process a recorded deed?
sections.html:
Documents delivered on paper are processed within four weeks of receipt, and documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state clerks' authority are processed in two to three business days. The clerk's site also carries a land records update page that reports progress on processing, so check it when timing matters for a closing.

After recording and processing, the original documents come back to you by mail. That gap is wide enough that you should ask whoever runs your closing how they plan to submit the deed. The clerk names three vendors: SimpliFile, eRecording Partners Network and Corporation Service Company (Ingeo).

sections.h2: What does the Fulton County clerk charge to record real estate documents?
sections.html:
A deed or any other instrument pertaining to real estate costs $25.00. Each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment is also $25.00 per instrument listed on the filing. The Real Estate Division does not accept credit cards for real estate transactions; it takes cash, business checks and money orders.

Fulton County clerk real estate fees (Fulton County Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts, fee schedule dated July 1, 2024)
ItemFee
Deed or other real estate instrument$25.00
Cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment (per instrument)$25.00
Plat, map or floor plan, per page$10.00
UCC filed in real estate records$25.00
Lien or General Execution Docket recording$25.00

The same schedule lists other recording lines, such as $5.00 for the first page of an instrument not otherwise specified, so ask the division which line fits your document before you send payment.

sections.h2: How is Georgia transfer tax collected on a Fulton County sale?
sections.html:
No deed gets recorded here until transfer tax is settled. The state charges a flat $1 on the first $1,000 of price, then a dime for each further $100 or fraction thereof.

Responsibility falls on the seller by default, and a clause in the sales contract can hand it to the buyer. The PT-61 declaration is filed online through the clerks' authority, whose support line for filers is (800) 304-5174. Whether a given transfer is exempt is a question for this clerk, according to the state.

sections.h2: How do I search or copy Fulton County land records?
sections.html:
Visit the Deeds and Records Room and use its computer lab, or search from home on the state authority's website, which the clerk says costs $5 for four hours of access. Staff cannot do legal research by phone. For questions about a deed or lien index, you either search it yourself or hire a title search company.

  • Certified copies must be ordered through eCertification at ecert.gsccca.org, which delivers a secure PDF by email after you approve payment.
  • Plain copies can be ordered the same way, around the clock.
  • By mail, send a letter naming the document type and its book and page number. The clerk's FAQ lists $1.00 a page for plain copies and $2.50 for the first certified page plus $0.50 for each added page.

If you cannot find a recorded cancellation of your old loan, ask your servicer for a copy and then check the index.

sections.h2: What do tax liens and tax appeals cost at the Fulton County clerk?
sections.html:
Tax liens filed by a state or local agency have their own pricing: $5.00 for page one, $2.00 for every page after, and $2.00 more for each cancellation, release, notice or withdrawal that references the original. Federal tax liens, materialman's liens, lis pendens and writs of fieri facias fall under the $25.00 lien and General Execution Docket line instead.

Property owners who take a county tax appeal to superior court will find a $25.00 County Tax Appeal line in the clerk's court-cost table. The assessor's notice and the board that hears the first appeal come before that step, so start with the county's assessment office and the notice it mailed you.

Transfer tax is billed on top of every figure above. If the deed is the only thing you are recording, the $25.00 fee and that tax are the two numbers to plan around.

sections.h2: What about intangible recording tax and foreclosure sales in Fulton County?
sections.html:
A lender financing the buyer's purchase pays a separate intangible recording tax, which the state prices at $1.50 for every $500 of the note, with part of $500 counted as a whole.

Foreclosure sales are a separate public process. The clerk's FAQ says properties sold in Fulton County are advertised once a week for four weeks in the legal notices of Fulton Neighbor Newspapers. Auctions run monthly on the first Tuesday, with bidding hours from 10:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps.

  • Anyone behind on a mortgage should get the scheduled sale date from the servicer in writing.
  • A sale that has already been advertised still leaves time to sell the property or work out a plan, but that window is short.

sections.h2: What does the Fulton County housing picture look like for sellers?
sections.html:
Fulton County is a large urban county with over a million people. Census Bureau QuickFacts shows 1,098,791 residents in July 2025 across 526.70 square miles of land, with 534,663 housing units. Owners occupy just 54.3 percent of the homes, which leaves rentals as a big slice of the market.

Owner-occupied homes carry a median value of $458,800 in the 2020 to 2024 survey, set against median gross rent of $1,732 a month. Median household income was $95,292. Builders pulled 9,660 permits in 2025. The county counts 462,481 households averaging 2.26 people each.

Sellers of a rental or inherited house should line up the recorded deed history before listing, because a missing cancellation or an old lien is easier to clear before a buyer's title search finds it.

faqs.q: Which Fulton County office takes a deed for recording?
faqs.a: With the Real Estate Division of the Fulton County Clerk of Superior and Magistrate Courts in Atlanta, or through an approved eRecording vendor. The customer service number is (404) 613-5313.

faqs.q: How much is the Fulton County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: The fee schedule dated July 1, 2024 lists $25.00 for a deed or any instrument pertaining to real estate, plus $25.00 for each cancellation, satisfaction, release or assignment.

faqs.q: Does the Fulton County clerk take credit cards for real estate recording?
faqs.a: No. No. Pay with cash, a business check or a money order.

faqs.q: How quickly does Fulton County record a deed?
faqs.a: Paper documents are processed within four weeks of receipt. Documents sent through an eRecording vendor or the state authority are processed in two to three business days.

faqs.q: When are foreclosure sales held in Fulton County?
faqs.a: Monthly, on the first Tuesday, with sales running 10:00 a.m. through 4:00 p.m. at the courthouse steps. Notice appears weekly for four weeks beforehand, per the clerk's FAQ.
